doc.title: Frank Foster — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

chapter: Joining Basie and life on the road
title: The Basie bus and the band's 1953 roster
summary: Foster describes the bus and seating and names the trumpets, trombones, saxes and rhythm section.

story.theme_name: Life on the road: touring bands, buses and one-nighters
story.community_name: Life on the road: buses, trains and one-nighters

blocks.x: It’s interesting. How was the bus? What was the bus like? Just a regular old bus?
It was a regular old Greyhound-type bus that you could grab the windows and just push them open like that.
Was there anything unique or special about it, or it was just a bus?
Did people have places they sat? Was it -­
Everybody in the band had a designated seat in which he or she sat. They had a female vocalist named Bixie Crawford. I think she sat right behind Basie.
When you joined the band who was there at that point?

In the trumpet section were Joe Newman, a gentleman by the name of Paul Campbell -- they used to call him Uncle Cam -- Wendell Culley, a very distinguished looking and acting person from Worchester, Mass., who spoke perfect English and was a gentleman and always wore a suit and tie. I said Joe Newman, right? The lead trumpeter was a person called Renauld Jones. Trombones were Henry Coker, Benny Powell, and the composer-arranger Johnny Mandel. The saxophones were Marshall Royal, Frank Wess, Ernie Wilkins, Charlie Fowlkes on baritone, and myself.
So at that point Jimmy Wilkins had left the band?
Yes, he had left the band before I joined.

On bass was a gentleman by the name of Gene Ramey I think, either Gene Ramey or Al Hall. My memory is hazy there. And of course Freddie Green, Count Basie, and Gus Johnson was the drummer. Now proceed.
